candidates.exact_span: Sample frequency is based on the March, 2012, NMIP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Anchors monitoring frequency obligations to the NMIP; how the NMIP is applied could change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span:
Based on the
discharge frequency of the facility, the NMIP requires that pH has daily monitoring frequency
and all other limited parameters have weekly monitoring frequency requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets parameter-specific monitoring frequencies and identifies which parameters are 'limited'; different readings of discharge frequency or the limited-parameter set could change applicable limits and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span:
Flow is
proposed to be monitored daily by estimate.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes flow as a daily estimate-monitoring obligation rather than grab-sample monitoring; interpretation affects whether flow monitoring was required and what kind of evidence (estimate vs numeric sample) is expected for missing-result analysis.

candidates.exact_span:
Grab sample type is proposed because a discharge
would be the overflow from a retention pond.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies proposed sample type for routine monitoring; a different interpretation of sample-type requirements could change which monitoring obligations apply.

candidates.exact_span:
Procedures for implementing WET terms and conditions in NPDES permits are contained in the
NMIP, March 2012. Table 11 of Section V of the NMIP outlines the type of WET testing for
different types of discharges.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporates NMIP Table 11 for WET test-type selection by discharge classification; interpretation of discharge type or NMIP cross-reference could change applicable WET limits and monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span:
The 48-hour WET testing for toxicity will be maintained for the
proposed permit term. The frequency is 1/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines WET test duration and annual frequency; different readings of test type or frequency could change enforceable WET limit comparisons and whether annual WET monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span:
The CD of the discharge was previously
determined to be 100%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a categorical dilution determination for WET; interpretation of CD applicability affects which numeric WET limit applies for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The test species shall be Daphnia pulex.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the WET test species; a different species interpretation would change the applicable toxicity limit and the required monitoring protocol.

candidates.exact_span:
During the period, beginning at the effective date of the permit and lasting through the expiration
date of the permit, the permittee is authorized to discharge from Outfall 001 to the Corral
Canyon.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the authorized outfall, receiving water, and permit term window; interpretation affects where and when discharge-related monitoring and missing-evidence expectations attach.

candidates.exact_span: WET testing is established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Locates WET obligations at Outfall 001; interpretation affects which discharge point's limits and monitoring requirements are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span:
Because there was no data to analyze WET
RP therefore conditions from the last permit will be carried over.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Carries forward prior-permit WET conditions due to missing RP data; interpretation affects which WET limits apply, whether current monitoring obligations are fully specified, and how the missing-data state is classified.

candidates.exact_span:
WET will be performed at first
discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Makes WET monitoring conditional on discharge occurrence; interpretation affects whether WET was required during no-discharge periods and how absent WET results are characterized.

candidates.exact_span:
A grab sample type is established because if a discharge occurs, it comes from a
retention pond which provides a relative similarity of effluent characteristics and EPA does not
expect such a discharge will last long.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes grab-sample requirements for WET when discharge occurs; interpretation could change applicable WET sampling obligations.

candidates.exact_span:
2. Discharges are restricted to overflows from the retention pond due to catastrophic or
        chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricts when discharges may occur; interpretation affects whether discharge-triggered monitoring was required and whether periods without overflow qualify as documented no-discharge or conditional non-monitoring periods.

candidates.exact_span:
3. Discharges of storm water runoff from access roads in undisturbed areas shall be
        covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns access-road stormwater to a different permit; interpretation affects whether monitoring obligations and missing-evidence expectations under this permit apply to those flows.

candidates.exact_span:
4. If a discharge of storm runoffs from mining areas is necessary, the discharge must
        comply with effluent limitations established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links mining-area storm runoff discharges to Outfall 001 effluent limitations; interpretation affects which numeric limits apply to that discharge pathway.

candidates.exact_span:
The applicant is required to operate the treatment facility at maximum efficiency at all times; to
monitor the facility’s discharge on a regular basis; and report the results quarterly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes general monitoring and quarterly reporting obligations beyond parameter-specific frequencies; interpretation of 'regular basis' and quarterly reporting could change applicable monitoring requirements.
